title: Tesla Full Self-Driving v12 may have driven owner Max Paul Franklin 13 miles to a Veterans Affairs emergency room during an insulin-pump failure at 2 a.m. in North Carolina
summary: Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 drove Max Paul Franklin 13 miles to a VA emergency room at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024, according to his own uncorroborated post on X.
account: By his own account, Max Paul Franklin, a North Carolina television producer, had severe dehydration at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024. His blood glucose read 670 after his insulin pump malfunctioned. He says that he got into his Tesla Model Y and engaged the Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 trial unlocked the day before. He says that it drove the 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention and offered to park. Il Fatto Quotidiano names the hospital as the Charles George VA Medical Center in Asheville. He reports a mild heart attack and discharge with no restrictions. He posted this account on X on 10 April 2024. Tesla and Elon Musk reposted it on 11 April 2024. No hospital or official source has confirmed it. The Office of Defects Investigation of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) raised Franklin's post with Tesla at a meeting on 15 April 2024 and in an email of 14 May 2024. It wrote that Tesla's repost conflicted with Tesla's own message that drivers must keep control. NHTSA published the email in November 2024 and did not rule on whether the drive took place. Owner accounts of similar rescues on 15 November 2025 and 18 February 2026 appeared in 2026.
purpose: Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is built to navigate a Tesla to a chosen destination while an attentive driver supervises it. Driving Franklin to the destination that he set is that function. Use by a driver impaired by a medical emergency is not an intended use. Hindustan Times notes that the system depends on driver intervention when needed. A Tesla owner quoted by Tesla Oracle calls it a Level 2 system. It requires hands on the wheel and eyes on the road even when active.
system: Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 on a Tesla Model Y
model_version: FSD v12 (Supervised), unlocked on the car on 1 April 2024 per Franklin and Tesla Oracle; the exact build is not stated (The Driven describes the then-current release as 12.3.3)
domain: Road transport / access to emergency care
segment: Consumer driver-assistance software on a privately owned vehicle
taxonomy_note: The documented good is transport to emergency care; no health outcome is reported.

ratings.reason: By his own account Franklin reached a VA emergency room during an insulin-pump failure with blood glucose at 670. He says that he was treated for a mild heart attack and left the hospital with no restrictions, which is a serious condition treated in time. No clinician, hospital or official source confirms the emergency or the drive.

ai_role.statement: The only description of what FSD did is Franklin's. Engaged by a double click of the stalk, it drove 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention and offered to park on arrival. No Tesla vehicle data, dashcam footage, hospital record, emergency-service log or official statement has been found. No outlet reports having interviewed him or the hospital. Tesla's corporate account and Elon Musk reposted the story on 11 April 2024 but added no facts. The photos attached to the post are two hospital-bed selfies and a night shot of a Model Y in a wet car park. They show no route, timestamp or hospital name. Some syndicated coverage garbles the story (Sky TG24 places him in Virginia and describes low blood sugar). The counterfactual, calling emergency services, driving himself or not reaching care, is unexamined. Commenters cited by Il Fatto Quotidiano argued he should have called for help.

fields.purpose: Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is built to navigate a Tesla to a chosen destination while an attentive driver supervises it. Driving Franklin to the destination that he set is that function. Use by a driver impaired by a medical emergency is not an intended use. Hindustan Times notes that the system depends on driver intervention when needed. A Tesla owner quoted by Tesla Oracle calls it a Level 2 system. It requires hands on the wheel and eyes on the road even when active.

The post thanks the Charles George VA Medical Center team, and Il Fatto Quotidiano places the center in Asheville. fields.summary: Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 drove Max Paul Franklin 13 miles to a VA emergency room at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024, according to his own uncorroborated post on X.
fields.account: By his own account, Max Paul Franklin, a North Carolina television producer, had severe dehydration at 2 a.m. on 2 April 2024. His blood glucose read 670 after his insulin pump malfunctioned. He says that he got into his Tesla Model Y and engaged the Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12 trial unlocked the day before. He says that it drove the 13 miles to the VA emergency room without intervention and offered to park. Il Fatto Quotidiano names the hospital as the Charles George VA Medical Center in Asheville. He reports a mild heart attack and discharge with no restrictions. He posted this account on X on 10 April 2024. Tesla and Elon Musk reposted it on 11 April 2024. No hospital or official source has confirmed it. The Office of Defects Investigation of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) raised Franklin's post with Tesla at a meeting on 15 April 2024 and in an email of 14 May 2024. It wrote that Tesla's repost conflicted with Tesla's own message that drivers must keep control. NHTSA published the email in November 2024 and did not rule on whether the drive took place. Owner accounts of similar rescues on 15 November 2025 and 18 February 2026 appeared in 2026.
